title: Customer insight briefing and prioritized asks - Sep 2025
content:
Purpose:
This is a working synthesis of customer feedback collected from support tickets, CS voice-of-customer interviews, and sales handoffs (Aug–Sep 2025). Goal is to produce a short list of actionable feature asks with rough impact indicators and recommended next steps for product and engineering. Draft — notes + open questions included.

Methodology & scope:
- Sources: ~45 CS tickets flagged as "product-ask", 6 post-onboard interviews, 2 enterprise discovery calls, summer NPS follow-up.
- Time window: 2025-08-01 to 2025-09-10.
- Filtering: removed pure docs/clarity requests; kept asks tied to production/ops/SLAs.

High-level themes (ranked by frequency + explicit ask intensity):
1) Per-route cost and latency attribution (high frequency, high pain for growth SaaS)
2) Predictable capacity controls / pre-warming for dedicated pools (enterprise customers)
3) Better private/on‑prem onboarding checklist + deploy runbooks (security/regulatory customers)
4) Streaming partial responses + customizable flush cadence (real-time apps)
5) Model fallback controls & rollout observability (A/B, canary rollback automation)

Representative customer quotes:
- "We need to know exactly which routes are burning tokens — right now cost mysteriously spikes and we can't map to feature flags." — mid-market search product
- "Our inference peaks are short but intense; pre-warm or reserve capacity otherwise requests time out." — fintech customer
- "Onboarding private deployment felt like 6 months of ping‑pong; a prescriptive runbook would have saved us weeks." — healthcare ISV

Prioritized asks (short list) — rationale and recommended owner:
A) Route-level token + latency breakdown (CS score: 9/10)
- What: UI + API that shows tokens, latency P50/P95 per route, and per-model unit cost calculation.
- Why: Customers currently do manual attribution; high churn risk from bills that don't reconcile to product metrics.
- Rough impact: Reduces billing disputes, lowers support volume.
- Who: product-hosted-api + observability.
- Asks/notes: Consider a CSV export and a per-token-explanation API for billing automation.

B) Dedicated pool pre-warm / reserve API (CS score: 8/10)
- What: Simple API to reserve N instances for a time window + soft pre-warm trigger.
- Why: Enterprise customers need SLAs during predictable peaks and want to avoid slow scale-up.
- Rough impact: Prevents multi-minute cold-starts and reduces failed requests during spikes.
- Who: dedicated + platform-engineering.
- Tradeoffs: cost model for reserved windows; billing UI change required.

C) Private deploy onboarding runbook + checklist (CS score: 7/10)
- What: Step-by-step runbook, troubleshooting checklist, and a small runbook-run session offer from SE.
- Why: Multiple customers reported multi-week friction on networking, KMS, and audit setup.
- Who: private-deployments + solutions-engineering.
- Quick win: templated Terraform snippets + a "preflight" validation tool.

D) Streaming control knobs (flush window, partial token hooks) (CS score: 6/10)
- What: Let customers tune flush cadence and receive partial tokens for lower-latency UX.
- Who: serving-runtime + console-and-tooling.
- Open questions: default safe settings, SDK compatibility.

E) Rollout observability + explicit fallback policies in UI (CS score: 6/10)
- What: Show canary metrics, auto-fallback when quality regresses, easy rollback button.
- Who: product-console + optimize.

Confidence & frequency notes:
- Route-level billing/latency requests appear across small and mid-market customers; very sticky ask.
- Dedicated pre-warm is concentrated in enterprise + fintech/ads verticals with predictable peaks.
- Private deploy runbook is a low effort, high satisfaction win — frequent asks during onboarding.

Open questions / research tasks:
- How many customers would pay a small premium for guaranteed pre-warmed windows? (sales to run 3 quick intel calls)
- Is there existing telemetry that can drive route-level attribution without schema changes? (observability team to audit)
- What SDKs must change for streaming flush knobs? (dev-ex to assess)

Immediate next steps (owner + timeline proposals):
- Week 1: Product-hosted-api to draft PRD for route-level billing (owner: Priya K., target: 2025-10-02)
- Week 2: Dedicated engineering to spike pre-warm API (owner: Carlos M., target: 2‑week spike)
- Week 2–3: Private deployments + SE to assemble onboarding runbook and Terraform templates (owner: Liam O., deliverable: runbook v0)
- Continuous: CS to route customers asking for these features into JIRA epic CS-2345 and tag with "billing-visibility" or "pre-warm".

Notes to self / conversation fragments to follow up:
- Need to sync with billing infra about token pricing granularity — they may insist on hourly buckets.
- Ask growth ops for a short customer survey: would they accept an in-console toggle for reserve windows?
- Investigate whether existing metrics pipeline already has per-route token counts (if so, "low lift").

Appendix: short triage table (ask, frequency, pain, quick effort estimate) — quick summary for exec readout:
- Route billing: freq=high, pain=high, effort=medium
- Pre-warm: freq=medium, pain=high (for some), effort=medium-high
- Private runbook: freq=medium, pain=medium, effort=low
- Streaming knobs: freq=low-medium, pain=medium, effort=medium
- Rollout UI/fallback: freq=low, pain=low-medium, effort=medium

End — please add any missing quotes or tickets below; will fold into v1 and route to PRD owners.

Unresolved: Recommend a short stakeholder readout next Wed (2025-09-17) with Product + Eng reps to align on which two asks to prioritize for Q4 roadmap.
